between: Research has shown that identification of symptoms with a persistent, non-remitting character is possible at PHC level, even in resource-
limited settings. A persistent, non-remitting cough was uncommon in this study but was almost exclusively (88.9%) associated with TB.
Source: Marais BJ, Gie RP, Obihara CC, et al. Well defined symptoms are of value in the diagnosis of childhood pulmonary tuberculosis.

labels: Weight loss or failure to thrive
It is important to check the child’s weight, record it and compare with previous weights. Poor
weight gain can be defined in any of the following ways:
Î very low weight (weight-for-age (WFA) below −3 Z-score);
Î confirmed weight loss (more than 5%) since last visit;
Other causes of chronic lung disease
Clinical features that suggest other causes of chronic lung disease include:
Î generalized lymphadenopathy, oral thrush and parotid enlargement – HIV infection;
Î finger clubbing – lymphoid interstitial pneumonitis or bronchiectasis;
Î recurrent cough or wheeze responsive to bronchodilators – asthma.
